hypothesis: Operand B of the EX ALU is effectively hardwired to the immediate field: the ALU-B source mux in ex_stage selects id_ex_imm for register-operand instructions too (id_ex_alu_b_sel is mis-driven / tied so the rs2/forwarded-rs2 path is never reached), and the feed-forward of a forwarded rs2 is applied on the wrong node so it can never override the immediate. The same dead B-operand feeds the EX branch comparator, so the loop-exit condition in bench_ooo_overlap64 never fires, PC walks off the program into the 0xa5a5a5a5 fill (0xc24..0xc5c), the ECALL never retires, and halted times out at 6000 cycles. constraints: Do not rename or change the direction/width of any port in the interface contracts (rv32i5, if_stage, id_stage, ex_stage, mem_stage, wb_stage, hazard_unit, forwarding_unit).
Forwarding priority: EX/MEM (forward==2'd1) beats MEM/WB (forward==2'd2); never forward when the producer rd or the consumer source field is x0.

ALU-B for R-type/I-type operand instructions MUST select the (forwarded) rs2 value; ALU-B selects id_ex_imm only for U-type/JAL and store-data uses rs2; apply the forwarding mux on the rs2 value BEFORE the alu_b_sel immediate substitution s

I-type/S-type/B-type immediates must be sign-extended from instr[31:20]/instr[31:25]|instr[11:7]; U-type from instr[31:12]<<12; J-type sign-extended from instr[31:12]; stop using the malformed {instr[31:21],1'b0} zero-extended slice.
Keep single-cycle memory model (no added wait states), synchronous active-low reset, and dmem_valid = mem & rst_n & ~halted gating unchanged.
Do not modify teacher TB, spec, or scoring scripts.
verification_targets: t02_alu_r passes: x4 == 0x0000000b (OR), x16 == 0x00000001 (SLT), x17 == 0x00000001 (SLTU) — i.e. R-type results use the real rs2 operand, not rs1<op>0.
t03_alu_imm passes: x3 == 0xfffff7ff (ADDI -2049) — sign-extended I-immediate, not 0x000007fe.
t04_upper passes: LUI/AUIPC produce the U-immediate<<12 (e.g. x1 == 0x12345000, x6 == 0x80000000).
t05_forward passes: x2 == 0x0000000f, x3 == 0x00000014, x4 == 0x0000001e, x5 == 0x0000000f, x7 == 0x00000002, x13 == 0x00000054 — forwarding chain resolves to the produced values.
bench_ooo_overlap64 reaches halted==1 within the cycle budget (no 6000-cycle timeout; imem_addr no longer stuck at 0x28 / walking 0xc24..0xc5c fill).
rejected_hypotheses: (1) EX-stage spurious redirect for non-control instructions: ex_redirect/branch/jump qualifiers leaking into PC load — rejected because re-application left identical register values.
(2) id_stage immediate-type mis-decode alone — rejected: fixing only the immediate expression cannot fix R-type/forwarding/branch failures whose operands are register-sourced.
(3) wb_stage/regfile commit-path mis-wiring — rejected: results are per-opcode-consistent with a zeroed/imm B operand, not random landed registers.
(4) ALU-B select polarity inversion alone in ex_stage — rejected: polarity flip without fixing the forwarding-mux ordering still leaves rs2 unreachable and immediate malformed.
(5) ID/EX payload capture / imm slice {instr[31:21],1'b0} — partially confirmed for t03 but insufficient alone; the ALU-B path still never selects rs2 so t02/t05/branch remain broken.
(6) regfile second read port / top-level rs2 wiring — rejected: repairing rs2 read cannot help while ALU-B is stuck on the immediate path.
